note: Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, 07:02 SGT -- before Asia's open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30 SGT). Monday 12 Oct's US equity session is now the latest completed close (S&P -0.06%, Nasdaq -0.44%, Russell -0.45%, VIX +2.49% to 15.21, a modest pullback after Friday's rally). CNN's Fear&Greed API again returned HTTP 418 to automated fetch and no search result cites a Monday-dated value distinct from Friday's 45 -- carried forward unchanged (45, Neutral) as the honest read given Monday's near-flat price action. Two mirror sites (fearandgreedgraph.com) gave two DIFFERENT readings (46, then 48) for the same page on repeated fetches within the same session, and neither mirror's own historical series matches CNN's recorded history -- rejected as unreliable, same category of problem as the previously-flagged Trefis conflict. Crypto Fear&Greed WAS genuinely updated via alternative.me's direct JSON API: the latest posted daily print (Oct 12 00:00 UTC) is 69 (Greed), up from 61 -- some secondary crypto-news headlines cite a conflicting 'drops to 56' figure from roughly the same window, but those are paraphrased/secondary and are not used here; the direct primary API reading of 69 is published as the authoritative value, with the conflict noted. A conflicting Barchart snippet (70.51/65.60) was traced to a probable technical-rating/index-value conflation and rejected. Advancers/decliners and 52wk highs/lows found no trustworthy fresher print (a circulating '8 highs vs 7 lows' figure was rejected as an index-level/constituent-count confusion) -- carried forward unchanged. McClellan Oscillator has a tentative, not-Monday-dated estimate (~+20 to +27, last observed ~Oct 9, up from a prior negative reading) -- labeled explicitly as last-observed, not a fresh Monday close. Flows: confirmed no newer EPFR/BofA Flow Show or ICI weekly edition has posted since the week-ended-Oct-7 print; next editions remain due ~Oct 14 (ICI) and ~Oct 15-16 (EPFR) -- carried forward.

flows.narrative: The full BofA/EPFR weekly print landed with a much clearer and, in several cases, quite different picture than Friday's preliminary approximations. Headline: a record $166.4B flooded into money-market funds -- the largest weekly inflow since April 2020 -- with Hartnett framing it as structural cash-hoarding ('no rate cuts, no reduction in cash') rather than a classic flight-to-safety, since money funds already offer attractive yields. Bonds added $33.8B. Global equity funds still took in a net $12.4B even so: US equities swung back to a modest inflow (+$3.3B, first in three weeks), EM funds logged a second straight week of inflows (+$2.1B), helped by China-dedicated funds rebounding sharply as domestic investors returned from Golden Week, and Europe barely held positive (+$0.2B, second straight week). Japan was the standout loser, flipping to its biggest outflow since May (-$3.3B). Gold ETFs added a steady +$2.0B, continuing the record-setting 2026 run even as spot gold hit fresh highs Friday. Within US sectors, Technology funds took in $3.5B (largest in six weeks) while Financials saw their biggest outflow since March (-$3.0B). No newer weekly edition has been published as of Monday pre-open; the next one is expected ~Oct 15-16.
